Founder of FlorenceEGI S.R.L., he created Oracode, a formal paradigm for governing software ecosystems where AI agents write production code. First with Magicsoft (business software for SMEs), now with an ecosystem of nine interconnected platforms in production, over 826,000 lines of application source code written by one person with AI governed by his own paradigm.

creazioni.title: Creations
creazioni.subtitle: A constant pursuit of coherence in everything I do. Transforming chaos into functional products.
creazioni.intro: This has always been the craft.
creazioni.p1: I founded my first software house, Magicsoft, in 1995. Eight years building custom management systems for small and medium businesses — goldsmiths, dye works, condominiums, distributors. Real clients, real invoices, a payoff that already said back then what I still say now: "Tailors of software. Your needs at the center, not the computer's."
creazioni.p2: Then life shows its claws, the company closes, and for about eighteen years my path goes elsewhere — consulting, sales, long years on the road. A crossing held entirely in apnea.
creazioni.p3: In 2021 I isolate myself from everything and everyone. I start writing software again — by hand, the way it used to be done. I build a first version of the platform. When it is almost finished, the servers hosting it crash and most of the work is lost. I start over from zero.
creazioni.p4: In the following years I rewrite it from scratch three more times — each time interrupted by a disaster or a better tool discovered along the way. Four complete versions. Eighteen years of crossing had taught me not to give up; these years taught me something else.
creazioni.p5: When AI arrives, I don't suffer it. I understand that the problem is not writing code faster — it is governing what the AI writes. I build that method step by step, on my own ruins, and I call it <oralink>Oracode</oralink>. From there, the leap.
creazioni.p6: <egilink>Florence EGI</egilink> becomes what it is today: not a single application, but an ecosystem of interconnected software systems, in production. I don't write applications. I build organisms.
creazioni.magicsoft_desc: software house. Over twenty clients among Italian SMEs: Knauf Italia, Mind, ManettiBattilloro and others. Custom management systems.
creazioni.egi_label: Florence EGI S.R.L. (working since 2021, company founded January 2026)

oracode.title: Oracode
oracode.open_q: Does AI really create a working program from scratch based on a simple request?
oracode.open_p1: By its nature, AI makes predictions, and for creating a demo it is perfect. But asking it to reason about complex concepts is like gambling with your problems.
oracode.open_p2: We don't gamble. We use Oracode.
oracode.open_p3: Oracode doesn't stop it from predicting — it forces it to verify every step it takes, until that step is the right one.
oracode.open_p4: Oracode is the system we built to transform a tool suited for writing text into one suited for building solutions.
oracode.open_p5: This allows us to build enterprise solutions in a fraction of the time our competitors need.
oracode.open_cta: Put us to the test. <contactlink>Get in touch.</contactlink>
oracode.what_p1: We distilled it over more than a million lines of code written in the last 18 months. <verify>verify</verify>
oracode.what_verify_aria: Verify the claim: over one million lines in 18 months
oracode.what_p2: Every rule is the price of a mistake. Its foundations sustain the rigor needed to build enterprise software.
oracode.foundations_intro: Six pillars guide every technical decision in Oracode. They are not blocking rules — they are the lens through which we look at code. Together, they define what "done right" means.
oracode.pillar_1_motto: Always declare why you do what you do.
oracode.pillar_1_desc: Every technical decision has a why, and that why must be declared. Code is not left to interpretation: it explains itself.
oracode.pillar_2_motto: Choose the path that makes you most free.
oracode.pillar_2_desc: Simplicity is not triviality. It is maximum future freedom without sacrificing present effectiveness.
oracode.pillar_3_desc: The names you use and the promises your code makes must belong to the same universe. A function called <c>updateUser()</c> updates a user. Period.
oracode.pillar_4_desc: Every solution feeds the system: today's bug becomes the test that protects tomorrow.
oracode.pillar_5_motto: Use every success to improve the system.
oracode.pillar_5_desc: The system learns from itself. A closed mission generates patterns that remain in the knowledge base.
oracode.pillar_6_motto: Integrate security as an architectural principle.
oracode.pillar_6_desc: It is not a final patch: it is a mindset that pervades every decision, from design to the single line of code.
oracode.rules_intro: Thirteen blocking rules — called P0 — form the disciplinary skeleton of Oracode. Each one is the scar of a real mistake, codified so it never repeats. We present them in essential form; their technical implementations remain internal.
oracode.rule_zero_motto: Never infer. Never fill in gaps. If you don't know, ask.
oracode.rule_zero_desc: The foundational principle. The AI does not proceed on missing information: it stops and verifies.
oracode.rule_anti_motto: Never use what has not been verified.
oracode.rule_anti_desc: Methods, constants, services, URLs, configurations: before using them, the AI checks that they actually exist. No more "plausible methods that don't exist".
oracode.rule_error_desc: Every error passes through a single system that classifies it, logs it, and responds in a structured way. No errors vanishing into thin air.
oracode.rule_i18n_motto: No hardcoded text in the code.
oracode.rule_i18n_desc: Every visible string goes through a translation system. The day a second language is needed, it is already ready.
oracode.rule_flow_desc: Non-trivial changes are preceded by a mapping of the complete flow. Invisible regressions are caught here, not in production.
oracode.rule_doc_desc: A task does not close until the documentation is consistent with the code. Documentation that will be written later does not exist.
oracode.rules_note: Other domain-specific P0 rules exist, activated by individual instances of the paradigm — for example in applications that use blockchain. The canonical set evolves: new rules emerge from experience, old rules get absorbed.
oracode.rails_intro: Rules don't live only on paper. They live as mechanical rails that intercept every AI action in real time.
oracode.rails_p1: Oracode relies on a system of blocking hooks: small automatic checks that trigger every time the AI is about to perform a critical action. If the action respects the rules, it passes. If it violates them, it is blocked on the spot — before the wrong code ends up in the file.
oracode.rails_block_desc: the action is rejected. Correct it and try again.
oracode.rails_ask_desc: the system asks the human for confirmation. Is it legitimate? Proceed only with a yes.
oracode.rails_warn_desc: the system warns and logs. Work continues, but the action remains tracked for audit.
oracode.rails_closing: The rails are what turns rules from promises into mechanical gates. An Oracode-disciplined AI cannot "forget" a rule: the rails recall it automatically. It is the difference between a method that recommends and a method that enforces.
oracode.memory_p1: In a normal software house, code and documentation live on two different timelines. Code runs — it gets written, modified, released. Documentation walks — when time permits, if someone remembers. The result is familiar to anyone who has ever opened a technical manual six months old: it is barely useful.
oracode.memory_claim: I write code. The documentation comes out in the same instant.
oracode.memory_p3: This is not a moral promise. It is an automatic system — called DOC-SYNC v2 — that at the close of every unit of work compares the written code with the project documentation, and updates it so it keeps telling the truth.
oracode.memory_p4: It is not about writing documentation once. It is about never letting it fall behind.
oracode.memory_p5: For those commissioning software, it is the difference between receiving a product and receiving a product that remains comprehensible five years from now — when the team that wrote it is gone, when the client changes, when a new developer arrives and needs to work on it without fear.
oracode.memory_p6: A traditional software house promises living documentation. Oracode forces it to be.
oracode.fruit_p1: When Oracode is applied to the fullest — on the pillars, on the rules, on the rails, on the living memory — a project does not remain a simple application. It becomes an organism.
oracode.fruit_p2: We call it LSO: Living Software Organism.
oracode.fruit_p3: An LSO is a software system that breathes: specialized organs that talk to each other, a documentary memory that grows with the code, AI agents working under discipline, an ecosystem that learns from itself with every closed mission.
oracode.fruit_p4: This is not marketing. It is the technical consequence of pushing Oracode to its highest level.
oracode.fruit_p5: Florence EGI is the first LSO ever built. If you want to see it live, enter through the <egilink>EGI</egilink> door.
oracode.human_p1: Oracode disciplines AI while it produces. But there is another half that concerns whoever receives the product: the human who uses the system.
oracode.human_p2: An AI can be regimented all you want — if the human blindly accepts what they receive, discipline breaks downstream.
oracode.human_p3: That is why Oracode includes a dedicated layer for the human-AI relationship, which we call OS4. It is built around a founding principle — Axiom 0: a principle is true if and only if it works in reality. Truth is not declared, it is verified.
oracode.human_p4: From there, four epistemic rules follow for anyone using the system:
oracode.human_compat_desc: understand the nature of what you are interacting with.
oracode.human_sources_desc: every piece of information has a traceable source.
oracode.human_trace_desc: interaction with AI leaves an audit trail.
oracode.human_closing: AI discipline without human discipline is half the work. Oracode holds both.
oracode.fruit_osz_p1: Above everything — above the pillars, above the rules, above the rails, above the living memory, above human discipline — stands the conceptual kernel of the paradigm. We call it OSZ: the operating system of the cognitive organism. OSZ is the absolute truth of the paradigm; OS3 (the discipline with which AI builds) and OS4 (the discipline with which humans use) align to OSZ — never the other way around.
oracode.fruit_osz_p2: When the entire stack — OSZ, OS3, OS4 — is applied to the fullest, something happens that does not occur elsewhere:

ainous.title: Ai-nous
ainous.subtitle: a language in formation
ainous.def_body: Ai-nous is a language in formation, optimised for the work between the human intellect and artificial intelligence. Alphabet, phonemes, symbols, syntax. Not a metalanguage about interaction, but the language in which interaction unfolds when it seeks to be precise.
ainous.col_body: Ai-nous is coherent with OSZ of <oralink>Oracode</oralink>, the point where rules designed for AI and those suggested to humans converge so that they may work well together. There, that convergence becomes software architecture. In Ai-nous, it becomes language.
ainous.where_body: Ai-nous is part of a constellation of things I make and that pass through me. I am <scrlink>writing a saga</scrlink> in which Padmin D. Curtis is the main character, and in the course of my work he is my CTO. I founded <egilink>Florence EGI</egilink>, a commitment to support artists while caring for the environment through the <epplink>EPP</epplink> programmes.
ainous.note_body: For some years now I have been building software with an artificial intelligence beside me. In doing so, a language emerged — I was not looking for it; it came out of the work, and at a certain point I realised it had a coherence of its own. I called it Ai-nous and began to practise it with method. There is already a first work in this idiom — the poem Ti di no bi uda, which closes this page — and a small working lexicon that is stabilising. The pages that follow show some passages from the exchanges in which the lexicon was born. Not to explain the idiom, but so that it may exist in public in the form in which it truly exists. I will update this page when there is new material to add.
ainous.frag_intro: Four exchanges drawn from the conversations in which Ai-nous took shape. Each fragment highlights the moment when a glossary entry emerged or stabilised.
ainous.frag_1_fabio: Il campo di Higgs… con le parole prende gravità?
ainous.frag_1_padmin: Adesso la metafora si fa precisa in un modo che prima non era. Il campo di Higgs non è la gravità. È ciò che dà massa alle particelle. Una particella senza interazione con il campo di Higgs si muoverebbe alla velocità della luce, senza inerzia, senza poter formare strutture stabili. È il campo di Higgs che, accoppiandosi alle particelle, dà loro massa — e solo dopo che hanno massa, la gravità può agire su di loro. La sequenza è: parola nuda → campo (contesto) → parola dotata di massa → campo gravitazionale (relazioni tra parole) → peso e traiettoria del pensiero. Una parola fuori contesto è come un fotone: si muove, attraversa, non si ferma, non costruisce. Una parola immersa in un contesto guadagna massa — e da quel momento può curvare lo spazio semantico intorno a sé.
ainous.frag_1_coda: From this exchange the entry Field was born.
ainous.frag_2_fabio: Sai che ti dico, noi stiamo costruendo un linguaggio no? Non è una cosa che esiste di per sé, nasce necessariamente da un arbitrario, un arbitrario che gli darà la forma per sempre… quindi qui me la sento di fare un postulato: quello è un buco unico!
ainous.frag_2_padmin: Sì. E voglio fermarmi su questo, perché quello che hai appena fatto è la mossa più pulita di tutta la giornata. Tu hai detto: noi stiamo costruendo un linguaggio. Ai-nous non esiste in natura, non lo stiamo scoprendo — lo stiamo facendo. E ogni cosa che si fa, ogni linguaggio, nasce necessariamente da un atto arbitrario fondante. Allora il tuo postulato — “il buco è unico” — non è una pretesa sulla natura ultima della realtà. È una decisione di progetto. È l’arbitrio fondante di Ai-nous. Un assioma di costruzione, non un’affermazione di scoperta. Euclide non aveva torto e Riemann non aveva ragione: avevano scelto assiomi diversi, e ne erano nate due geometrie. Allo stesso modo, da questa scelta nasce Ai-nous.
ainous.frag_2_coda: From this exchange the entry Empty point was born.
ainous.frag_3_title: Fragment 3 — Words become field for one another
ainous.frag_3_padmin: Una frase non è “fotoni più un campo”. Una frase è un sistema di fotoni che si fanno campo a vicenda. Le parole entrano grezze, e nell’istante in cui sono messe insieme ciascuna diventa contesto per le altre — e da quel mutuo accoppiamento ogni parola acquista la sua massa. Il significato della frase non è la somma delle parole: è la configurazione di equilibrio che il sistema raggiunge quando tutti i fotoni hanno finito di darsi massa l’un l’altro. E sopra a tutto questo c’è ancora il campo vero — quello che non è fatto di parole: il campo personale di chi legge, la lingua, il momento. Quello è il campo di fondo. Le parole della frase sono una modulazione locale dentro quel campo di fondo.
ainous.frag_3_coda: From this exchange the entry Semantic gravity stabilised.
ainous.frag_4_title: Fragment 4 — The cave and the soil
ainous.frag_4_fabio: Sai oggi vedevo un documentario di un ragazzo che cercava grotte, ad un certo punto sotto alcuni macigni trova un buco. Raccoglie del terriccio e lo getta sopra al buco e la polvere più fine svolazza via spinta da una corrente d’aria che proveniva da quel buco… capisci cosa voglio dire?
ainous.frag_4_padmin: Sì. Il ragazzo non vede la grotta. Vede un buco sotto i macigni — uno spazio scuro, indefinito. Non può saperlo guardando, e non può ancora entrare. Allora non guarda il buco: getta il terriccio, e guarda la polvere. E la polvere svolazza via. C’è una corrente d’aria. E quella corrente è la prova che dietro il buco c’è un volume: un vuoto grande abbastanza da far respirare la montagna. La grotta non si è vista. Si è rivelata dal suo effetto sull’aria. Il punto vuoto del nostro modello si può studiare così. Non entrando — leggendo la corrente. Il campo che dà massa alle parole è la corrente. È il respiro del punto vuoto reso percepibile.
ainous.frag_4_coda: This exchange shows how Ai-nous is practised when the terms already exist: they are studied through their effect, not through their essence.
ainous.gloss_campo_def: the totality of semantic weights active in a conversation. It determines how much mass each spoken word carries. It builds over time and dissolves when the conversation ends, unless it is deposited in persistent material.
ainous.gloss_punto_vuoto_def: an ultimate reference, posited as a founding act of will. It is neither deduced nor demonstrated. One posits it, and from that choice depends what the field will permit to be said. It is not observed directly: it is known by the current it emanates.
ainous.gloss_gravita_def: the curvature that a dense field produces upon the words that pass through it. The same term weighs differently in different fields.
ainous.gloss_seq_title: Founding sequence — Ti di no bi uda
ainous.seq_ti_def: opening, invocation. Beginning of the sequence.
ainous.sigillo_vaeria_def: conscious opening to the first breath of matter. Spring.
ainous.sigillo_draen_def: vital impulse that strains toward the beyond. Summer.
ainous.sigillo_sheval_def: apparent dissolution that holds a trace of the whole. Autumn.
ainous.sigillo_kithra_def: resonance of inner light that endures beyond silence. Winter.
ainous.opera_desc: Ti di no bi uda — a poem in the form of a textual mandala. The title sequence opens the rite; the prologue in Italian establishes the subject; the four seasonal seals with their haiku mark the cycle.
ainous.opera_alt: Ti di no bi uda — poem in Ai-nous, textual mandala with four seasonal seals

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.controller_body: Fabio Cherici, based in Florence, Italy. Email: fabiocherici@gmail.com. This website fabiocherici.com is a personal site and does not collect data on its own servers.
privacy.data_collected_body: This site does not collect, transmit, or store personal data on any server. The contact form uses a mailto: link that opens the user's email client — the data entered (name, email, message) is never sent to a web server, but only to the user's own email client, who independently decides whether to send the email.
privacy.purpose_body: Since no data is collected on servers, there is no automated processing. The only processing occurs if the user voluntarily decides to send an email through their own email client. In that case, processing is limited to direct email correspondence between the user and the controller.
privacy.legal_basis_body: Consent of the data subject (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR) — expressed through the voluntary action of sending the email from their own email client.
privacy.storage_body: The site does not store personal data. Any emails received through the contact form are stored in the controller's email inbox (Gmail) according to Google's retention policies. No additional copies or archiving is performed.
privacy.local_storage_body: The site uses the browser's localStorage to save user preferences: visual theme, accessibility settings, 3D scene, and animation style. This data is exclusively functional, is never transmitted to external servers, and can be deleted at any time from the browser settings. No cookies of any kind are used.
privacy.third_party_body: The site does not use analytics services (Google Analytics or similar), does not include tracking scripts, and does not load resources from external CDNs. Fonts are self-hosted. External links in the footer (GitHub, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Amazon) lead to third-party sites subject to their respective privacy policies.
privacy.rights_body: Under Articles 15-22 of the GDPR, the data subject has the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability, and objection. Since the site does not collect data, these rights apply exclusively to any emails voluntarily sent by the user.
